title: Nebraska's 2nd Congressional District election, 2026 (open seat)
description: An open-seat race for Nebraska's 2nd Congressional District after Republican incumbent Don Bacon announced he would not seek re-election in June 2025. The Omaha-based district, known as the 'blue dot' for voting Democratic in the last two presidential elections while electing a Republican House member, is one of the most competitive House seats in the country and a key Democratic target for flipping control of the U.S. House. The Democratic primary was won by Denise Powell, co-founder of Women Who Run Nebraska, while Republican Brinker Harding, an Omaha city councilman, ran unopposed for his party's nomination. The general election will also feature Libertarian Eric Michael Foreman, with the race rated as Lean Democratic by the Cook Political Report as of mid-2026.
polling_note: No public general election polls were found for the Harding-Powell matchup as of June 2026. The New York Times maintains a polling tracker for this race but no independent polls with published margins have been reported yet.

candidates.name: Denise Powell
candidates.summary: Denise Powell is a small business owner and co-founder of Women Who Run Nebraska, a political action committee that supports women running for local office. She won the Democratic primary on May 12, 2026, defeating state senator John Cavanaugh in a closely contested race. Her campaign focuses on lowering costs, protecting health care and public schools, defending reproductive rights, and cleaning up corruption in Washington.

candidates.name: Brinker Harding
candidates.summary: Brinker Harding is an Omaha City Council member representing District 6 since 2017 and a commercial real estate broker. He ran unopposed for the Republican nomination and was endorsed by President Donald Trump. His campaign emphasizes restoring America's founding principles, public safety, economic growth through public-private partnerships, and bringing Omaha's balanced-budget approach to Washington.

candidates.summary: Eric Michael Foreman is a Libertarian candidate for Nebraska's 2nd Congressional District. He works in property management and maintenance and is a high school graduate with additional education in culinary arts, trade skills, and applied sciences. He advanced from the Libertarian primary unopposed.

forecast.rationale: This open-seat race for Nebraska's 2nd Congressional District is one of the most competitive House seats in the country, but structural fundamentals give Democrats a modest edge. The district (Omaha's 'blue dot') voted Democratic in the last two presidential elections, and Republican Don Bacon's retirement removes the GOP incumbency advantage that had historically allowed ticket-splitting. Cook Political Report rates the race Lean Democratic as of mid-2026. Democrat Denise Powell won a competitive primary against state senator John Cavanaugh, while Republican Brinker Harding ran unopposed with an endorsement from President Trump. Harding is a credible, well-funded candidate with city council experience, and the district has repeatedly shown willingness to elect Republicans down ballot despite its presidential lean. No public general election polls exist for this matchup, so the forecast relies entirely on structural signals and ratings — hence low confidence. The Democratic advantage is real but limited rather than commanding, consistent with a lean Democratic rating.
